title: Cello
summary: Cello notes played through a computed cello body. Limits first: A3 still drives a 16-mode steel laboratory plate, not a cello (its fixed lines at 41, 149 and 283 Hz are the plate's); the low notes are too dark, the notes too clean, and the stopped notes sit off pitch. The other notes drive a computed spruce and maple shell body with an air cavity, a finite-width hair bow, the measured rosin friction law of Woodhouse and Galluzzo (2025, eq. 13) and the printed 116 mm after-length. E2 and E3 sit 8.5 and 7.7 c flat of equal temperament after one finger move, and F5 holds a line at a third of its pitch. Eb4 is rendered at 47944 Hz to remove time-step lines, which leaves it too clean. D3 keeps 512 body modes, the others 256.
physics_present: a computed cello shell body from published plate geometry and wood data: spruce top, maple back and ribs, a 12.5 mm-class table, a 19 g bridge and 256 computed modes (D3 keeps 512, its last mode about 4.3 kHz)

an enclosed air cavity through a physical neck, and f-holes placed from printed caliper measurements of the Castelbarco Stradivari (Library of Congress); the C2 page's physics list does not name the f-holes
the measured Kaplan string rows (Mansour 2016): tension, mass, bending stiffness and loss factors for the string played, with the bridge and bow flexibility
a bow of finite width (a 10 mm ribbon) with hair compliance, driven by a gesture schedule of ramp, hold and lift; on D3 the bow force follows the bow speed through the start of the stroke
the measured rosin friction curve (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13) on every note except A3, which uses the hyperbolic law
the printed 116 mm after-length, bridge to tailpiece (Fouilhe and Houssay, SMAC 2013), on every note except A3

stopped notes: a rigid finger stop on the fingerboard (Issanchou 2017) at 1e12 N/m on the C string (E2, E3) and 1e13 N/m on the A string (F5, and Eb4 as its page), placed at the equal-tempered station and then moved once toward the named note, never toward the recording, on E2, E3 and F5; Eb4's finger is not moved
Eb4 rendered at 47944 Hz, a rate chosen so its period is a whole number of samples, and resampled to 48 kHz for the page
physics_missing: a measured cello: the body is computed from published geometry and wood data, and no measured body admittance or string Q of this instrument is on the cards; on the C2 page the wood data are stated only from 150 Hz (maple) and 100 Hz (spruce), so that body has no mode below 150 Hz, above the C2 fundamental
A3 on a cello body: it still plays the 16-mode laboratory plate, and the plate's fixed lines are not a cello's
body modes above the computed range: 256 modes end at 2438.5 Hz (D3's 512 at about 4.3 kHz); the plates are resolved to about 3 kHz and the ribs not above about 1 kHz

body damping: the shell's lowest strong pole reads Q 78 from wood alone, against 18 to 26 printed for a cello on a rig or foam and 13.4 held by a player (Zhang and Woodhouse 2014); the F5 page names this as a likely reason for its fault, not shown
a body-radiation skin row: the posted cards carry none

a bow that varies during the note: force and speed hold after the ramp (D3's force follows speed only through the start), so the notes repeat too exactly: harmonics-to-noise reads 63.9 dB on Eb4 against 37.9 in the recording, 43.4 against 30.1 on E2 and 37.4 against 30.1 on C2; the Eb4 attack is far too quick, 22 ms against 411

time-step independence: at 48 kHz a note's period can lock to the render clock and put lines into the sound that are not in the instrument; Eb4 needed its own render rate, and F5 still holds a line at exactly a third of its pitch (233.0 Hz, -28.8 dB)

an explanation of the finger: the bowed pitch moves 1.4 to 1.8 times the length of the move (E3 25.3 c for 17.6 c, E2 19.2 c for 10.7 c), so E2 and E3 land flat of equal temperament, and the E3 and F5 recordings sit sharp of it

the timbre balance: the low notes are too dark (centroid 245 Hz against 388 on C2, 185 against 390 on E2, 215 against 575 on E3) and Eb4 and F5 too bright (604 against 466, 1936 against 1187); D3's first two harmonics are swapped (H2 7.7 dB over H1, the recording 7.5 dB under); on F5 the third harmonic leads with the first 15.7 dB under it, the recording the other way
lines that are not harmonics: C2 shows two about 18 dB over the recording (163.9 and 174.8 Hz), untraced
the other strings: only the bowed string is on a card, so there is no sympathetic ringing and no string-to-string coupling through the body
the rosin's temperature-dependent behaviour, transfer layer and contact history: eq. 13 is a velocity law measured at steady sliding
blocked: A3 plays the 16-mode laboratory plate; it waits on a cello-body A3 render that replaces it.
